schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE USER (UID INT, UNAME INT, CITY INT);
CREATE TABLE PICTURE (UID INT, SIZE INT);
q1: SELECT P.UID, P.UNAME, COALESCE(Q.CNT, 0) AS CNT FROM (SELECT X.UID, X.UNAME FROM USER AS X WHERE X.CITY = 3) AS P LEFT JOIN (SELECT Y.UID, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM PICTURE AS Y WHERE Y.SIZE > 1000000 GROUP BY Y.UID) AS Q USING (UID)
q2: SELECT X.UID AS UID, X.UNAME AS UNAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM USER AS X, PICTURE AS Y WHERE X.UID = Y.UID AND Y.SIZE > 1000000 AND X.CITY = 3 GROUP BY X.UID, X.UNAME
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.UID, P.UNAME, COALESCE(Q.CNT, 0) AS CNT FROM (SELECT X.UID, X.UNAME FROM USER AS X WHERE X.CITY = 3) AS P LEFT JOIN (SELECT Y.UID, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM PICTURE AS Y WHERE Y.SIZE > 1000000 GROUP BY Y.UID) AS Q USING (UID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.UID AS UID, X.UNAME AS UNAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM USER AS X, PICTURE AS Y WHERE X.UID = Y.UID AND Y.SIZE > 1000000 AND X.CITY = 3 GROUP BY X.UID, X.UNAME
counterexample: INSERT INTO USER (UID, UNAME, CITY) VALUES (1, 1, 3);
explanation: Q1 uses a LEFT JOIN to count the number of pictures for users in city 3, while Q2 uses an INNER JOIN and a WHERE clause to achieve the same. Q1 will include users in city 3 with no pictures in the result, while Q2 will not.
counterexample_dsp: A user in city 3 with no pictures.
